extracted.intended_audience: General readers of Esquire interested in celebrity insights, life lessons, and humorous/witty quotations
extracted.subtask_description: A magazine feature that collects short, pithy 'what I've learned' quotations from well-known figures (actors, musicians, leaders, scientists, etc.) as a curated anthology/anniversary roundup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose distinguished actors, musicians, world leaders, scientists, and business leaders ("Giants. Legends. Leaders. Innovators.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The series pulls from a wide roster of notable figures — examples include Jack Nicholson, Rodney Dangerfield, Ted Williams, Ray Charles, Muhammad Ali, and newcomers for the anniversary such as Johnny Depp and Eric Clapton. Aim for recognizable, authoritative, or culturally interesting voices whose brief observations carry weight or charm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content type: condensed life lessons, knowledge, and weird insights
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect short, pithy statements that distill life lessons, knowledge, or quirky observations (the page explicitly: "condensed life lessons, knowledge, and weird insights").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are brief one-liners or short sentences suitable for rapid reading and quotation. Emphasize clarity, wit, and memorability — e.g., "Silence is golden when you can't think of a good answer." or "Music is about the only thing left that people don't fight over."

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial approach: minimal framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid lengthy introductions or heavy editorializing — "No introduction to what you're about to read could possibly add anything to the experience... You just get out of their way."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let the voices speak for themselves; provide minimal connective text. For an anniversary or roundup, brief explanatory framing is acceptable, but the feature's value comes from the quotations themselves rather than extended commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: witty, candid, and often irreverent
rubrics_metrics.description: The collected quotations tend toward humor, bluntness, and candid appraisal (many entries are comedic or provocative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include remarks that are funny, surprising, blunt, or provocatively honest. Examples on the page range from self-deprecating to sharp-edged humor (e.g., Rodney Dangerfield: "Never tell your wife she's lousy in bed..."). Balance comedic lines with occasionally serious or reflective observations for variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Each quotation is followed by a brief attribution (name, role/title, age or descriptor, and city) as the standard presentation format on the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise attributions like: 'Michael J. Fox — Actor, 46, New York City'. Maintain consistent formatting for readability in a list/compilation context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and cadence: serialized monthly feature, suitable for anniversary compilation
rubrics_metrics.description: The feature is a recurring monthly column ("Every month for the last ten years") and can be compiled into larger anniversary editions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual monthly items should be short and standalone; anniversary roundups may assemble many entries (this piece collects 180 contributors) and can highlight new voices among established ones.
